sentences.text: Learned counsel for the petitioner contends that the petitioner has been falsely implicated in the present case.

He argued that the alleged agreement to sell was executed on 16.09.2021 but the FIR in question was registered on 16.08.2025 i.e.
afier an unexplained delay of more than 03 years, casting serious doubt on the prosecution story.

He further CRM-M-11316-2026 argued that even as per prosecution case, there is no element of cheating involved in the present case as it is conceded in the FIR itself that on 09.07.2023, the petitioner/seller duly informed the complainant that she was not in a position to execute the agreement to sell.
He further argued that an amount of Rs.1 lakh was also returned to the complainant due to the rescission of the said agreement to sell.

He argued that if the contents of the FIR are taken to be true, even then the dispute in the present case is of civil nature,
which has been given criminal colour by registering the present FIR.

He further Simmi Sharma vs State Of Punjab on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/90124237/
1 argued that no offence under Section 420 is made out against the petitioner as the contents of the FIR, even on face of it do not fulfill the ingredients of cheating in any manner.

5. In view of the statement made by learned State counsel, the interim order dated 26.02.2026 is made absolute.
The petitioner shall continue to join investigation, as and when called by the Investigating Officer and shall also abide by the conditions as provided under Section 482(2) of the BNSS.
